interfaccia.why: Banco CAD is laid out like SolidWorks: commands at the top, tree on the left, part in the middle.
steps: At the top there is the [[CommandManager]]: the **Features**, **Sketch**, **Evaluate**, **Drawing** and **Assembly** tabs change the buttons shown below.
On the left there is the [[Albero di progettazione]]: planes, origin and all the features in the order you made them.
When you create or edit a feature, the [[PropertyManager]] with its parameters takes the place of the tree; ✓ confirms, ✕ cancels.
In the middle there is the 3D view; at its top, the small bar with Fit, orientations, display style, section and planes.
At the bottom, the status bar tells you what is selected and, in a sketch, whether it is defined.
The **Guide** and **Glossary** buttons at the top open this guide and the dictionary of terms; the small ⓘ next to panel titles explains that item.
**Project › User manual (PDF)** opens the complete [[Manuale d'uso|manual]], to read or print. It needs an Internet connection: if you want it always at hand, download it.
tips: Keep the Guide open while you work: the panel stays on the right and does not cover the tree.

vista.why: Look at the part from every side without changing it.
steps: **Mouse – wheel:** zooms towards the point under the pointer: forward zooms in, backward zooms out.
**Ctrl + wheel:** rotates the model around the vertical axis.
**Dragging:** left button on empty space to rotate; right button (or Shift + left) to pan.

**Tablet:** spreading or pinching two fingers zooms. To rotate and pan, **touch the part first** (the view border turns blue and «Part held» appears): then one finger rotates and two fingers pan. Touch empty space or «Release» to let it go.
**Keyboard:** space bar for the orientations (Front, Top, Isometric…), F to fit the part to the window.
tips: If you get lost, press Fit (the first button of the small bar at the top) and then Isometric.

primo.why: The basic path of every model: dimensioned sketch → feature.
steps: **Sketch** tab › **Sketch**, then choose the [[Piano superiore]] (for a plate) or the [[Piano frontale]].
Draw a **Corner Rectangle** with one corner on the [[Origine]] (the pointer snaps to it by itself).
With [[Quota intelligente]] click a side, click where to place the dimension and type the value; repeat for the other side.
When the sketch turns **black** it is [[Completamente definito]].
Press **Extruded Boss/Base** directly (Features tab): the sketch is confirmed automatically.
Type the [[Profondità]] and confirm with ✓.
tips: Shape first, dimensions second: there is no need to draw precisely, the dimensions set the sizes.

licenze.t: Viewing the licenses and the authors
licenze.why: Know what you can do with the program and who wrote its parts.
steps: Open the **Project** menu, at the top right.
Press **About and licenses**: you will find the [[GNU GPL 3]] license, the parts by other authors, the trademarks mentioned and the links to the texts.
tips: The program collects no data: your work stays in your browser.

lingua.why: Work with the command names of the English version of SolidWorks, or let people who do not speak Italian use Banco CAD.
steps: Choose **Progetto › Language: English**: your work is saved and the page reopens in English, with the same project.
To go back to Italian choose **Project › Lingua: italiano**.
In English numbers are written with a decimal point (12.5); in the fields you can also type a comma.
tips: The choice stays in this browser. A link to the site with ?lang=en at the end of the address opens the English version directly.
The names of features made in Italian (Estrusione1) are shown in English (Boss-Extrude1) without changing the project; a name you typed yourself stays as it is.

salvare.t: Saving, exporting and reopening your work
salvare.why: Never lose your work and take it to another computer.
steps: Your work **saves itself** in this browser at every change (even if you close the page).
To move it: **Project › Export project** and save the file (or copy the text).
On another computer: **Project › Import a project** and choose the file (or paste the text).
**Project › New project** clears the bench: export first if you want to keep the work done.
**Project › Export STEP** saves the part to open it in another CAD program (SolidWorks, Inventor, Fusion, FreeCAD…).
**Project › Export STL** creates the file for 3D printing.
**Project › Save PDF** creates a PDF of what you are looking at: the drawing, the open sketch or the 3D view.
tips: Automatic saving works for this browser and this device: to hand in a piece of work, use the export.
The project file (Export project) can only be reopened by Banco CAD; for other programs use STEP (3D part), DXF (2D drawing or sketch) or PDF (to read and print).

importa.t: Importing a part from an STL or OBJ file
importa.why: Use a part made with another program (SolidWorks, Inventor, Tinkercad…) to measure it, put it on a drawing or modify it.
steps: In the original program save the part as [[STL]] (or [[OBJ]]). In SolidWorks: File › Save As › type STL. If the program can write [[STEP]], use that: see «Importing a part from a STEP or IGES file».
Here: **Project › Import STL or OBJ** and choose the file.
Choose the [[Unità del file]] (usually millimeters) and, if the part arrives lying on its side, check [[Asse Z del file verso l'alto]]. Press **Import**.
**Imported1** appears in the tree: it is a [[Corpo a faccette]]. You can measure it, compute its mass (Evaluate tab) and put it on a drawing.
On its flat faces you can open a **Sketch** and add cuts, holes and extrusions, as on a part drawn here.
To change units or orientation: double-click **Imported1** in the tree.
tips: The part arrives without its feature history: the original dimensions cannot be edited.
If the [[Corpo chiuso|body not closed]] warning appears, the file has holes: volume and mass are not reliable.
At most 100,000 triangles; larger files must be simplified first.

importa-step.t: Importing a part from a STEP or IGES file
importa-step.why: Bring here, with its true surfaces, a part designed with SolidWorks, Inventor, Fusion, FreeCAD or another CAD program: to measure it, put it on a drawing or modify it.
steps: In the original program save the part as [[STEP]]. SolidWorks: File › Save As › type «STEP AP214 (*.step)». Inventor: Export › CAD Format › STEP. If only [[IGES]] is available, that works too.
Here: **Project › Import STEP or IGES** and choose the file (.step, .stp, .iges or .igs).
The unit of measure is written in the file: you do not have to choose it. If the part arrives lying on its side, check [[Asse Z del file verso l'alto]]. Press **Import**.
The first time, wait a few seconds: the reader ([[OpenCascade]]) gets ready. The file is read separately: meanwhile the page stays free, and with **Cancel** you can stop the reading.

If the file contains several bodies (an assembly), choose with the check boxes which ones to import ([[Corpi di un assieme]]). With **One «Imported» for each body** checked, each body becomes a feature of its own; otherwise a single **Imported1** appears in the tree.
The [[Facce del modello d'origine|faces of the model]] stay recognizable: on flat faces you can open a **Sketch** and add cuts, holes and extrusions.
Volume, area and mass (Evaluate tab) have an error well below 1 %. To change the orientation or turn off the [[Colori del file]]: double-click **Imported1**.
tips: The part arrives without its feature history: the original dimensions cannot be edited.
Each body of an assembly arrives in its own «Imported» feature (it can be suppressed or deleted on its own); with the box unchecked they all arrive in a single feature.
The face colors written in the file are shown on the part; the mass still uses the chosen material.
The .sldprt (SolidWorks) and .ipt (Inventor) files cannot be opened: save them as STEP first.
The reader is inside the page: it also works without the Internet.

sk-nuovo.t: Opening a sketch (on a plane or on a face)
sk-nuovo.why: Every feature starts from a 2D sketch.
steps: Select a plane in the tree (Front, Top or Right Plane) **or** a flat face of the part.
Press **Sketch**. If you have not selected anything, the program asks you to choose the plane.
The view turns [[Normale a]] the plane; the plane axes are dashed (X red, Y green, Z blue).
Draw, dimension, then confirm with ✓ (top right) or press a feature directly.
tips: On the face of a part the edges are shown in gray: you can snap and dimension to them ([[Geometria esterna]]).
Right-click a face or a plane › «Sketch on this plane».

sk-colori.t: Understanding the colors: blue, black, red
sk-colori.why: The color tells you whether the sketch is well defined.
steps: **Blue:** [[Sotto definito]] – some point can still be dragged; dimensions or relations are missing.
**Black:** [[Completamente definito]] – everything is fixed. This is the goal.
**Red:** [[Sovradefinito]] – there is one dimension or relation too many: remove the extra one: select it and press Delete, or remove it from the list of relations.
The status bar at the bottom repeats the state of the sketch.
Drag a blue entity to understand what is missing: it moves in the direction that is not yet constrained.
tips: Always tie the sketch to the origin (a dimension or a Coincident relation): otherwise it stays blue.

sk-linea.why: Outlines made of segments: L and T profiles, any polygon.
steps: Press **Line**.
Click for the first point, then click once for each following vertex.
To close the outline click the first point again (it snaps).
Double-click or Esc to end the chain.
In the panel on the left you can type [[Inserimento numerico|length and angle]] instead of clicking.
tips: If you draw a line that is almost horizontal or almost vertical, the Horizontal or Vertical relation is added by itself.

steps: **Corner Rectangle:** click one corner, then the opposite corner.
**Center Rectangle:** click the center (usually the origin), then a corner: the rectangle is symmetric.
Dimension one horizontal side and one vertical side with [[Quota intelligente]].
tips: With the center rectangle on the origin, two dimensions are enough to make it black.

steps: Press **Circle**.
Click the center, then a point on the circumference.
Dimension the diameter: [[Quota intelligente]] and click the circle (it becomes Ø).
Dimension the position of the center from the origin or from the edges.
tips: Several identical circles: [[Uguale]] relation, so one dimension is enough for all of them.

sk-archi.why: Fillets, slots, rounded profiles, sweep paths.
steps: **Centerpoint Arc:** click the center, the start point and the end point.
**3 Point Arc:** click the start, the end and a point in between.
**Tangent Arc:** click the end of a line (or of an arc), then the end point: the arc continues without a corner.
Dimension the radius with [[Quota intelligente]] (click the arc).
tips: For sweep paths always use the tangent arc: the path must have no corners.

sk-poligono.why: Hexagons for screw heads and nuts; slots for adjustments.
steps: **Polygon:** choose the number of sides in the panel on the left, click the center, then a vertex.
**Straight Slot:** click the center of the first arc, the center of the second, then click once for the width.
Dimension the distance between the centers and the width.

sk-mezzeria.why: Axes of revolution and of symmetry; helper lines that do not become material.
steps: **Centerline:** click the first and the second point. It is drawn dash-dot.
It is used as the axis for **Revolve**, for **Mirror Entities** and for the Symmetric relation.
**Construction Geometry:** select entities already drawn and press Construction Geometry: they become dashed and make no material (and the other way round).
tips: For a turned part, draw the centerline on the Y axis through the origin and half of the profile on one side.

sk-raccordo.why: Round or bevel a corner of the profile before extruding it.
steps: Press **Sketch Fillet** (or **Sketch Chamfer**).
Type the radius (or the distance) in the panel.
Click the vertex shared by two lines.
tips: To round the edges of a solid already made, use the [[Raccordo]] on the Features tab instead.

sk-taglia.why: Remove the extra pieces of line where entities cross.
steps: Press **Trim Entities**.
Click the part to remove: it disappears up to the nearest intersections.
Repeat until the outlines are closed and without crossings.
tips: An outline that crosses itself cannot be extruded: the red message says so.

sk-specchia.why: Draw half of the profile and get the other symmetric half.
steps: Draw a [[Linea di mezzeria]] and half of the profile.
Select the entities to copy and the centerline (Ctrl+click).
Press **Mirror Entities**: the copy has the symmetry relations.

sk-dxf.t: Importing a DXF or DWG drawing into a sketch
sk-dxf.why: Use the outline of a part drawn with another program (AutoCAD, DraftSight, LibreCAD, a SolidWorks drawing…) without redrawing it.
steps: Get the drawing as a [[File DXF]] or [[File DWG]]. If it has a title block, border or hatches, you can turn off their layers in the window.
On the tab: **Sketch › Insert DXF or DWG** (or **Project › Import DXF or DWG (sketch)**). Outside a sketch choose the **plane**; inside a sketch the geometry goes into the open one.

Choose the file: the window shows a **preview** of the drawing, with a small red cross on the point that will go on the origin. If the drawing has several [[Layer|layers]], uncheck the ones you do not need (title block, dimensions, border): the preview updates.

Choose the [[Unità del file]] (usually «from the file») and the **position**: as in the file, or with the lower left corner or the center on the origin. The **Texts, dimensions, hatches and tables as reference background** box brings them under the sketch, in gray ([[Sfondo del disegno]]): also the [[Tratteggio del disegno|hatches]], the [[Tolleranza geometrica|geometric tolerances]] and the [[Richiamo multiplo|multileaders]]. Press **Import**.

The entities arrive selected and blue ([[Sotto definito]]): check that the outlines are closed, then press ✓. [[Ellisse|Ellipses]] and [[Spline|splines]] arrive as chains of tangent arcs ([[Biarco|biarcs]]).

If you have the background, read the gray sizes and put them back with **Smart Dimension**: those in the file do not drive the shape. In the sketch panel you can hide it (**Show the background**) or remove it (**Remove the background**).
Select the sketch and use **Extruded Boss/Base**, or **Revolved Boss/Base** if there is a [[Linea di mezzeria]].
tips: Dash-dot lines in the file become centerlines, dashed lines become construction geometry (see [[Tipo di linea]]).
Very close end points are joined and double lines removed, so the outlines close.
If the part arrives 10 or 25.4 times larger or smaller, change the unit and repeat.
The final message says into how many arcs each ellipse or spline was divided, and the [[Scostamento dalla curva]]: usually a few thousandths of a millimeter.
You can also import whole drawings with thousands of entities; to keep only the part, uncheck the layers you do not need (title block, border, dimensions).
Layers that are off or frozen in the file start unchecked.

You can also choose a **.zip** with the DXF inside: that is how the DWG → DXF Converter saves files in the published page. If the zip holds several drawings (the converter's «Save all DXF» button), choose one in **Drawing in the zip**.
A **DWG** takes a moment longer, because it is first turned into a DXF: meanwhile the page stays free, and Cancel stops the reading.
To save DXF files, for other programs or for many drawings at once, there is the [[Convertitore DWG → DXF]].

sk-converti.why: Use the edges of the part in the sketch (for example for a boss on the border).
steps: Open the sketch on a face: the edges of the face are gray.
Select the gray edges you need.
Press **Convert Entities**: they become sketch lines tied to the part.

sk-quota.why: Give the sizes: lengths, distances, diameters, radii, angles.
steps: Press **Smart Dimension**.
**Length:** click a line. **Distance:** click two points or two parallel lines. **Angle:** click two lines that are not parallel.
**Diameter:** click a circle. **Radius:** click an arc.
Click where you want the dimension, type the value (expressions like 40/2 are fine too) and press Enter.
To change a dimension: double-click the number.
tips: If the dimension would turn the sketch red, it becomes a [[Quota condotta]] (in brackets): remove the extra constraint first.

sk-relazioni.why: Geometric constraints: parallel, perpendicular, tangent, equal…
steps: Select the entities (Ctrl+click for more than one).
Only the possible relations appear in the panel on the left: press the one you need.
The existing relations are listed in the panel: the × removes them.
With «Show the relations on the sketch» the symbols appear next to the entities.
tips: A relation in the right place is worth more than a dimension: for example Equal among four holes, or Horizontal between two centers.

estrusione.why: Give thickness to a closed profile: plates, blocks, bosses.
steps: Draw a closed sketch (holes inside are fine too).
Press **Extruded Boss/Base** (even while you are still in the sketch).
Choose the [[Condizione finale]]: [[Cieca]] with the depth, or [[Piano medio]] to get a part symmetric about the plane.
If needed: «Reverse Direction», [[Direzione 2]] to extrude to the other side too, [[Sformo]] to tilt the walls.
Look at the orange preview and confirm with ✓.
tips: The sketch to use is chosen from the «Sketch» list or by clicking its lines in the view.

taglio.why: Remove material: pockets, shaped holes, grooves, recesses.
steps: Make a sketch on the face where the cut starts (select the face › Sketch).
Draw and dimension the outline to remove.
Press **Extruded Cut**.
Choose [[Passante tutto]] to go through the part, or [[Cieca]] with the depth.
Confirm with ✓ (the preview is red).
tips: For standard holes (screws, counterbores, threads) use the [[Creazione guidata fori]].

sformo.why: Molded or cast parts: tapered walls let the part come out of the mold.
steps: Open an Extruded Boss/Base or an Extruded Cut with the [[Cieca]] condition.
Check **Draft** and type the angle (for example 3°).
Normally the profile gets smaller going away from the sketch; check «Draft outward» to make it larger.
Confirm: flat faces become tilted planes, cylinders become cones.
tips: Draft works with the Blind condition in one direction only.

rivoluzione.why: Turned parts: shafts, pins, bushings, knobs; grooves and slots.
steps: Sketch on the Front Plane: a [[Linea di mezzeria]] (the axis) and **half of the profile**, closed, all on one side of the axis.
Dimension the lengths and the distances of the points from the centerline (they are the radii of the part).
Press **Revolved Boss/Base** (or **Revolved Cut** to remove material).
Angle 360° for a full turn; less for part of a turn.
Confirm with ✓.
tips: If the profile crosses the axis an error appears: move it all to one side.

sweep.why: Bent tubes, handles, wire springs, seals: a profile that slides along a line.
steps: **Path:** in a sketch draw **tangent** lines and arcs (use Tangent Arc or Sketch Fillet at the corners). Confirm.
**Profile:** on a plane perpendicular to the path, at the point where the path starts, draw the closed outline (for example a circle). Confirm.
Press **Sweep**: profile and path are chosen automatically; if needed change them from the lists or with «Pick in the view».
Confirm with ✓. To remove material use **Swept Cut**.
tips: For springs and threads the path is a [[Elica e spirale]] curve instead of a sketch.
Example: path on the Top Plane starting from the origin, profile (circle) on the Front Plane centered on the origin.
The radius of the path arcs must be larger than the profile.

elica.t: Helix and spiral: springs and threads
elica.why: Helical springs, spiral springs, real threads: a profile that slides along a curve turning around an axis.
steps: **Circle:** open a sketch on the plane perpendicular to the spring axis (for example the Top Plane) and draw a [[Cerchio]] with the mean diameter of the spring. Confirm.
Press **Helix and Spiral**: in [[Definita da]] choose which sizes to give (for example [[Passo]] 10 and [[Rivoluzioni]] 5) and look at the orange curve. Confirm with ✓.

**Profile:** open a sketch on a plane through the start of the helix (with the circle on the Top Plane and [[Angolo iniziale]] 0° it is the Front Plane) and draw the wire: a circle centered on the start point of the curve. Confirm.
Press **Sweep**: the profile and the curve are chosen automatically (the curve can also be chosen from the «Path» list or by clicking it in the view). Confirm with ✓.
tips: The pitch must be larger than the profile, otherwise the coils run into each other and an error appears.
For a conical spring check [[Elica rastremata]]; for a flat spring choose «Spiral».
For a real thread use **Swept Cut** with a triangular profile on a cylinder.
The length of the wire is shown in the curve panel.

loft.why: Solids whose section changes: twisted blades, hoppers, transitions from a square to a circle, handles.
steps: **First profile:** in a sketch draw the first closed outline (for example on the Top Plane). Confirm.
**Other planes:** with [[Piano di riferimento]] create a parallel plane at the distance you want, one for each other profile.
**Other profiles:** on each plane draw its closed outline (one outline per sketch). Confirm each time.
Press **Loft**: the free sketches go into the [[Profili]] list in tree order. Click in the view to add or remove one; use the ↑ ↓ arrows to change the order.
Check the orange preview and confirm with ✓. To remove material use **Lofted Cut**.
tips: **Twisted blade:** draw the same profile on two or three planes, each time rotated by a few degrees: the loft joins them by twisting the blade ([[Svergolamento]]).
If the profiles have the same number of sides (for example two rectangles), each vertex joins its matching vertex and the faces stay separate.
Between a square and a circle the points are matched along the perimeter: the surface passes smoothly from one shape to the other.
Two profiles on the same plane do not work: each profile needs its own plane.

nervatura.why: Thin stiffening walls, for example in the corner of a bracket.
steps: Open a sketch on a plane that cuts the part where the rib goes (often the Front Plane or a mid plane).
Draw **just one line** (open) where the free edge of the rib must run. It does not need to touch the part: it is extended automatically.
Press **Rib**, type the [[Spessore]] and choose the side (mid plane or one side).
If the material goes to the wrong side use «Flip material side». Confirm with ✓.

fori.why: Holes for screws according to the standards: clearance, counterbored, countersunk, tapped.
steps: Press **Hole Wizard** and click the flat face where the holes go.
The sketch of the positions opens: click once for each center, then dimension the positions (for example from the gray edges). Confirm with ✓.
In the panel choose the [[Tipo di foro]], the [[Grandezza]] (M3…M20) and the [[Passante per vite|fit]].
Choose [[Passante tutto]], or [[Cieca]] with the depth. The standard diameters appear under [[Valori di norma]].
Confirm with ✓.
tips: The depth of blind holes is measured up to the start of the [[Punta a 118°]].
To change the positions: double-click the hole › «Edit the positions».

corpi.why: Keep separate solids inside the same part, to combine them later.
steps: Create the first solid, then a new feature that adds material (**Extruded Boss/Base**, **Revolved Boss/Base**, **Sweep** or an imported body).
In the panel uncheck **Merge result**: a new body is born, and it appears in the **Solid Bodies** folder of the tree.

With several bodies a new feature starts from **Feature Scope › Selected bodies** with **Auto-select** checked: it works on the bodies it touches. Uncheck it to choose them by hand, or choose **All bodies**. **Fillets and chamfers** work only on the body of the edge.

To repeat a whole body, in **Linear Pattern**, **Circular Pattern** or **Mirror** use the **Bodies to pattern** box (in the mirror **Bodies to mirror**, with **Merge solids** if you want a single body). While the panel is open, bodies and sketches can also be picked by name in the **tree** above the view.
In **Evaluate › Mass Properties** you find the data of each body; **Export STEP** writes one solid for each body.
tips: With «Merge result» checked the material joins the bodies it touches; if there is more than one body and it touches none, a new body is born.

combina.why: Make a part by joining, subtracting or intersecting bodies, like «Combine» in SolidWorks.
steps: Press **Combine** and choose the operation: **Add**, **Subtract** or **Common**.

Check the bodies in the panel, or click them in the view (you can also pick them in the tree with Ctrl + click before pressing **Combine**). For **Subtract** first choose the **main body**, then the ones to take away from it.
Confirm with ✓: a single body remains.
tips: If the bodies have no material in common, Common gives an error: check their position.

spostacorpo.t: Moving, rotating or copying a body
spostacorpo.why: Put a body in its place or make copies of it, without redoing the sketches.
steps: Press **Body-Move/Copy** and check the bodies.
Type the **rotation** (X, Y or Z axis through the origin and angle) and the **translation** in X, Y and Z. It rotates first, then moves.
For copies check **Copy the body** and type the **number of copies**: each one is moved from the previous one.

eliminacorpo.why: Remove the bodies you no longer need, for example those used for construction.
steps: Press **Body-Delete/Keep** and choose whether the chosen bodies are **to delete** or **to keep**.
Check the bodies and confirm with ✓.
tips: It is a feature in the tree: if you suppress or delete it, the bodies come back.

raccordo.why: Round or bevel the edges of the solid.
steps: Press **Fillet** (or **Chamfer**).

Click **all** the edges to work: they turn blue (a second click removes them). With **Tangent propagation** checked (it already is), one click is enough for a chain of edges that continue without a corner, for example the edge of a slot.
Type the radius (for the chamfer: distance, or distance and angle, or two distances).
Confirm with ✓: the edges are worked **together**. Where two fillets meet they blend into each other; where three meet at right angles the corner becomes a piece of a sphere.
tips: Put edges that touch each other in the same feature: the result is the one of SolidWorks.
On an inside (concave) edge the fillet adds material.
The edge of an elliptical or spline hole is a **curved edge**: one click is enough to pick all of it. The radius must be smaller than the radius of the curve at its tightest point.

serie-lin.why: Repeat holes or bosses in a row or in a grid.
steps: Press **Linear Pattern**.
In «Features to pattern» click a face of the feature to copy (or its name in the tree).
Direction 1: X, Y, Z axis or an edge of the part; type the distance (spacing) and the number of [[Istanze]].
For a grid check Direction 2 and fill it in the same way. Confirm with ✓.

serie-circ.why: Flange holes, spokes, teeth spread around an axis.
steps: Make the first hole (or the first boss).
Press **Circular Pattern** and choose the feature to repeat.
Axis: X, Y, Z or «From the part» and click a cylindrical face (its axis is used).
Number of instances and total angle (360° = spread over the whole turn). Confirm.

specchio.why: Copy features symmetrically about a plane.
steps: Press **Mirror**.
Choose the features to mirror (click one of their faces).
Choose the plane of symmetry: front, top, right or a flat face.
Confirm with ✓.
tips: If the part is centered on the origin, the standard planes are already planes of symmetry.

piano.why: Make sketches where there is no face: in the middle of the part, higher up, offset.
steps: Select a plane or a flat face, then press **Reference Plane**.
Type the distance; «Reverse» for the other side.
Confirm: the new plane appears in the tree and can be used for sketches.
**Sketch on the plane:** click its name in the tree (it turns blue in the view) and press **Sketch**. Or press **Sketch** without choosing anything and pick the plane in the panel.

modifica.t: Editing a feature or a sketch
modifica.why: The model is parametric: change a size and the part updates.
steps: **Double-click** the feature in the tree (or a face of the part): its panel opens again.
For the sketch: right-click the feature › «Edit Sketch» (or double-click the sketch under the feature).
Change the values and confirm: all the features after it are recalculated ([[Rigenerazione]]).
If a feature turns red it has an error: hover over it with the pointer to read why.

albero-menu.why: Organize the history of the part.
steps: Right-clicking a feature in the tree opens the menu.
**Suppress:** the feature stays but is not calculated (struck through). Useful for trying variants.
**Rename:** give clear names (e.g. «M6 fixing hole»).
**Roll back here:** the orange [[Barra di ripristino]] hides the features below it; you can insert a feature in the middle. «Roll to End» to go back.
**Delete:** removes the feature (and those that depend on it, after a confirmation).
Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+Y redoes.

massa.why: Know the volume, area, mass and center of mass of the part.
steps: **Evaluate › Material** tab: choose the material (steel, aluminum, brass, plastics…).
**Evaluate › Mass Properties**: volume, area, mass, center of mass and bounding box appear.
With «Material…» in the same window you change the material on the fly.
tips: Without a material the mass is calculated with a density of 1 g/cm³.

misura.why: Check distances, diameters and angles on the part.
steps: Press **Measure**.
Click one or two faces, edges or vertices.
The result appears in the panel; «New measurement» starts again.

sezione.why: See inside the part without changing it.
steps: Press **Section View** (also from the small bar of the view).
At the bottom choose the plane and move the slider to move the cut; «Reverse» changes the part that is removed.
«Close» removes the section.

assieme.t: Creating an assembly and inserting the parts
assieme.why: Put several parts together, each in its place. Everything stays in a single project, that is in a single file.
steps: Open the **Assembly** tab.
Press **Insert Part** and choose a part of the project, or a file (STEP, IGES, STL, OBJ or an exported project). The file is copied into the project.

The first part inserted is [[Parte fissa|fixed]]: in the tree it has (f) before its name. The others are free and show (-) as long as they still have [[Gradi di libertà dell'assieme|degrees of freedom]].
To add another copy of the same part, insert it again or use **Copy component** from the right-click menu.
tips: A STEP file with several bodies becomes one part for each body, in the positions of the file.
Fix or Float a component with the right button. If you drag a fixed component, only the view turns.
The copies are the same part: if you change the part, they all change together.

parti.t: Several parts in the same project
parti.why: Draw the parts of an assembly without leaving the project, and change them when needed.
steps: Press **New Part** on the Assembly tab, or **Project › Add a part**. The new part opens empty: draw it as usual.
To switch from one part to another use the list next to the name, at the top.
In the assembly, double-clicking a component opens its part. When you go back to the **Assembly** tab, the components update and the mates are recalculated.
tips: Undo works separately for each part and for the assembly.
**Project › Delete this part** also removes its components and cannot be undone.
**Project › New project** starts again from scratch: export first if you need the work done.
**Project › Export project** saves all the parts and the assembly in a single file.

sottoassiemi.why: Divide a machine into groups: you assemble the group once and reuse it whole.
steps: Press **New Assembly** and assemble the group, as usual.
Go back to the other assembly with the list next to the name.
Press **Insert Part**: the list also contains the group, marked «subassembly». Mate it like a part: choose the faces of its pieces.
tips: A subassembly is rigid, until you choose Make flexible with the right button.
The bill of materials opens the subassemblies and counts the real parts.
Interference Detection also checks the pieces inside the subassembly; with the «Treat subassemblies as components» box it checks it as one block.
An assembly cannot contain itself: it does not appear in the list.
Right-click the name of the assembly in the tree to delete it.

flessibile.t: Letting the pieces of a subassembly move
flessibile.why: Try a mechanism mounted inside the machine: a slide moves, a hinge turns, and the mates of the upper assembly can stop it.
steps: Insert the subassembly with **Insert Part**.
Right-click the component in the tree: **Make flexible**.
Drag one of its pieces with the mouse, or mate a face of one of its pieces to another component.
tips: Each copy has its own positions: the original assembly stays as it is.
**Make rigid** puts the pieces back where they are in their own assembly.
A subassembly inside a flexible one stays rigid.

tangente.why: Rest a cylinder, a sphere or a free-form shape on a plane, or a cam on a follower.
steps: Press **Mate** and choose the two elements: a plane, a cylinder or a sphere; with a free-form surface of a STEP file, a plane or a sphere.
Press **Tangent**. With a free-form surface it is already chosen.
With **Flip side** choose on which side they touch. Press ✓.
tips: On free-form surfaces the precision is that of the triangles of the file.
Cones and edges have no Tangent mate.

vitenelforo.t: Putting a screw in with one click on the hole
vitenelforo.why: Mount the fasteners without making the mates by hand.
steps: Press **Screw in Hole**.
Click the wall of the hole, near the opening the screw goes in from.
In the window check type, size and length, then press **Insert**.
tips: For a nut or a washer, click near the opening on the side where they go.
In a counterbored hole click the small hole, so the head rests in the counterbore.
A single Undo removes the piece and the two mates.

viti.t: Putting a screw in a hole
viti.why: Mount the parts with standard fasteners, without drawing them, and have them in the bill of materials.
steps: Prepare the hole in the part with the [[Creazione guidata fori]]: clearance, counterbored, countersunk or tapped, of the same size as the screw.
In the assembly press **Screws and Bolts**, choose type, size, length and material, then **Insert**.
Press **Mate**: **Concentric** between the shank and the hole, then **Coincident** between the underside of the head and the face of the part.
For each identical screw, insert it again: the bill of materials keeps a single row, with the right quantity.
tips: A screw in a tapped hole or in a nut shows up in Interference Detection marked «thread»: this is normal, because the thread is only indicated.
On the drawing, threads are drawn with the thin lines of ISO 6410, in section views too: there the hatching goes up to the thick line.
A countersunk screw rests on its cone: use Coincident between the top face of the head and the face of the part, with a countersunk hole of the same size.

accoppiamenti.why: Say how two components sit relative to each other: for example a pin in a hole with its head resting on the plate.
steps: Press **Mate**.
Click two elements of two different components: faces, edges or vertices. The free component moves at once.

Check the [[Tipo di accoppiamento|type]]: [[Accoppiamento coincidente|Coincident]], [[Accoppiamento concentrico|Concentric]], [[Accoppiamento parallelo|Parallel]], [[Accoppiamento perpendicolare|Perpendicular]], [[Accoppiamento a distanza|Distance]] or [[Accoppiamento ad angolo|Angle]]. Only those possible with the chosen elements are active.
If the part is turned the wrong way press **Flip alignment** (or **Flip side**, **Flip angle**).
Confirm with ✓. The mate appears in the tree: double-click to edit it, right-click to suppress or delete it.
tips: Coincident between two circular edges brings the two circles into contact, with the same center: handy for a screw in a hole.
If two mates contradict each other, the message is red and ✓ does not confirm. A mate that becomes impossible after a change stays in the tree with an exclamation mark.
[[Piani e origine]]: in the panel choose the component and press the plane or **Origin**. No faces are needed: a part can be placed on the plane of another.

When you change the sizes of a part, a chosen [[Vertice dell'accoppiamento|vertex]] is found again by itself. The exclamation mark stays only if it really disappears, for example after a chamfer right on that vertex.

Among the curved faces of a STEP file, cylinders, cones, spheres and tori are recognized. A free-form surface can only be used with **Tangent**, against a plane or a sphere: for the other mates choose an edge or a vertex.

sposta.why: Try out the movement of the mechanism or bring the parts closer before mating them.
steps: With the mouse: drag the component with the left button. It moves only in the degrees of freedom it has left, and the mates stay true.
To rotate, or on a tablet: press **Move Component**, choose **Move** or **Rotate** and drag the component.
To turn the view in the assembly, drag on empty space or on a fixed component, or hold down the wheel.
tips: Undo puts the component back where it was.
A component tied to others takes them along, if they can follow it.

calcoli-assieme.t: Mass and bill of materials of an assembly
calcoli-assieme.why: Know how much the assembled machine weighs, where its center of mass is and which parts are needed to build it.
steps: Give each part its material: open the part and use **Material** on the Evaluate tab.
On the Assembly tab press **Mass Properties**: mass, volume, area, center of mass and bounding box of the whole assembly, then one row for each component.
Press **Bill of Materials**: one row for each part, with quantity, material, mass of one piece and total mass.
tips: The center of mass is weighted by mass: a steel part counts almost three times as much as an identical aluminum one.
A part without material is calculated with a density of 1 g/cm³, and the window says so.
Components of the same part make a single row of the bill of materials.

esplosa.why: Show how the machine is put together, with the pieces moved apart along a direction.
steps: Press **Exploded View**.
Click the components to move, choose the direction **X**, **Y** or **Z** (**Reverse** for the opposite way) and type the distance, or drag a chosen component.
Press **Add the step** and go on with the other components, then ✓.
To be quicker: **Arrange automatically** puts the components in a row along the chosen direction, with the spacing you give.
In the tree, a click on **Exploded View** explodes or collapses it; a double-click edits the steps.
tips: The real positions do not change: mass and interferences are calculated on the assembled machine.
In the exploded view the mouse turns the view. Mate and Move Component collapse the view by themselves.
For a slanted direction press **Direction from a face** and click a face: flat, it goes along the normal; cylindrical or conical, along the axis.
Export STEP and Save PDF work on what you see.

tavola-assieme.why: Get the general drawing to hand in: views, numbered pieces and bill of materials.
steps: While in the assembly, open the **Drawing** tab: the assembly drawing opens (from a part, the part's drawing opens).
In the panel, **Assembly** group: **Bill of Materials**, **Balloons** and, if there is an exploded view, **Exploded isometric view**.
Dimensions, section, title block, PDF, SVG and DXF work as in the part drawing.
tips: Each balloon number is the same as its row in the bill of materials. Row 1 sits right above the header, as the ISO 7573 standard requires.

The balloons place themselves along the sides of the isometric view. To move one, drag it with the mouse: the line that links it to the part follows it. Choose the scale with the isometric view already in place.
In the section all the components have the same hatch.

interferenze.why: Find out before building that two pieces take up the same space, and by how much.
steps: Put the components in the position to check.
Press **Interference Detection**, then **Calculate**.
In the list each row gives the two components and the shared volume. Click a row: that volume is shown in red, even inside the pieces.
Fix the part or the mate and calculate again.
tips: Two faces in contact are not an interference: a pin with the same diameter as the hole is not reported.
With imported pieces (STEP, IGES, STL, OBJ) a very thin layer is marked «maybe just contact», because those pieces are made of triangles.
With very complex pieces the calculation can hold the page still for a few minutes.

autoverifica.why: Check that the program's calculations are right.
steps: Press **Self-check**.
The program rebuilds the test parts and compares volume, area, center of mass and bounding box with the values calculated by hand.
The table shows, for each test, the largest error (allowed up to 1 %).

tavola.why: The dimensioned technical drawing to hand in or print.
steps: Open the **Drawing** tab: the views appear in [[Metodo E]].
On the left choose the [[Foglio]] (A4, A3…) and the [[Scala]] (Automatic chooses the largest standard scale that fits on the sheet).
Check the views you need (from above, from the left… and the isometric view) and the [[Linee nascoste]].
If you want the isometric view in color, check [[Assonometria ombreggiata]]: the faces take the color of the part (also that of a STEP file), the other views stay as lines.
Drag the views to arrange them: the projected ones stay aligned with the front view.
Fill in the [[Cartiglio]] (title, author, class, drawing number).
**Fit the sheet** brings the whole drawing into the window; the wheel zooms the sheet in or out around the pointer.

quote-tavola.why: Put the sizes on according to the rules of technical drawing.
steps: **Overall dimensions:** adds in one go the largest sizes and the diameters of the circles.
**Dimension:** click an edge (length), a circle (diameter) or two points of the same view, then click where to place the dimension.
Dimensions can be dragged to arrange them; the «Dimensions» list on the left lets you delete them.
tips: Dimensions go on the orthographic views, not on the isometric view.

sezione-tavola.why: Show the inside of the part with hatching.
steps: Press **Section View** (Drawing tab).
Choose the view to section, the position of the cutting plane and the letter (A).
«Apply»: the view becomes the hatched section A-A and the trace of the plane appears in the nearby view.

stampa.why: Hand in the drawing on paper or as a file.
steps: **Save PDF:** the simplest way: a PDF file of the drawing, to scale, that opens and prints anywhere (see «Saving the drawing, the sketch or the 3D view as PDF»).
**Print / PDF:** in the print window choose «Actual size» or «100 %» to get the right scale, or «Save as PDF».
**Export SVG:** vector drawing at 1:1 scale.
**Export DXF:** for AutoCAD and other 2D CAD programs, with layers and line types.

pdf.t: Saving the drawing, the sketch or the 3D view as PDF
pdf.why: Have a file to hand in, send or print, that opens on any computer, tablet or phone.
steps: **Drawing:** on the Drawing tab press **Save PDF**. The PDF has the real sheet size (A4, A3, A2) and the drawing at 1:1 scale: lines, dimensions and title block stay sharp at any zoom.

**Sketch:** with the sketch open choose **Project › Save PDF of the sketch**. The sketch goes on a landscape A4, at the largest [[Scala|standard scale]] that makes it fit (for example 2:1), written at the bottom. Dimensions and colors are those of the screen.
**3D view:** outside the sketch and the drawing choose **Project › Save PDF of the 3D view**. The view goes in as it is on screen (orientation, style, zoom) on a landscape A4, on a white background.
In the shared page the file goes through the claude.ai save window; in the file opened from the computer it goes into Downloads.
tips: To print to scale, open the PDF and in the print window choose «Actual size» or «100 %» (not «Fit to page»).
The 3D view in the PDF is an image: for a sharp drawing to scale use the drawing.

step.t: Opening the part in another CAD program (Export STEP)
step.why: Continue the part in SolidWorks, Inventor, Fusion or FreeCAD, or send it to whoever has to make it.
steps: Choose **Project › Export STEP (for other CAD programs)**: the .step file holds the part as a solid, in millimeters.
In the other program open it with **File › Open** (in SolidWorks: STEP file type).

Planes, cylinders, cones, spheres and tori arrive as [[Superficie vera|true surfaces]]: in the other CAD program a hole has its exact diameter and a fillet its radius. The message says how many there are.
Surfaces that cannot be written exactly (two cylinders crossing each other, a sweep along a free curve) arrive divided into narrow flat faces: the solid stays closed.
tips: Dimensions and the feature history do not pass: no CAD program exchanges them with the others. New features can be added on top of the imported part.
Banco CAD reads its own STEP files back with Project › Import STEP or IGES.
